name: security-adcs-certificate-enrollment-review
intent: AD CS certificate template enrollment and identity authority
artifacts: Template settings, enrollment/management permissions, issuance requirements, EKUs and CA policy.
trace: Determine which low-privilege principal can enroll or modify a template and what identity/purpose a resulting certificate would represent.
experiment: Use an owned lab CA or configuration proof with synthetic identities; compare intended enrollment and an out-of-policy subject/purpose request.
disproof: A risky-looking template flag alone does not establish effective enrollment or certificate-based authentication to a protected service.
repair: Constrain enrollment/template authority and issuance identity, verifying intended certificate workflows and denied impersonation.
branch_decisions: Evaluate template enrollment rights, subject/SAN control, issuance requirements, EKUs and CA policy together. A permissive-looking template alone does not establish a usable authentication certificate. Use exported configuration or an isolated lab to trace the exact claimed principal and relying service; do not enroll certificates impersonating real directory users.
operational_method: Retain CA/DC build and patch level, template issuance/enrollment settings, certificate SID/strong mapping evidence and the actual relying authentication protocol. A SAN selected by a caller is not enough to decide accepted identity under current strong-mapping enforcement. Compare a deliberately mapped synthetic identity with a mapping-mismatched certificate in supplied traces or an isolated directory lab; certificate issuance, successful mapping and final service authorization are separate necessary edges. Do not request impersonation certificates for real principals.
